newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Christians' Lee steps down, recount unlikely.
newsitem.headline: NZ Christians' Lee steps down, recount unlikely.

text.p: New Zealand Christian Coalition co-leader Graeme Lee said on Thursday he was resigning his position as leader of the Christian Democrats and leaving politics.
While he expects the coalition to pick up special votes from churchgoers and Mormons who did not vote on Saturday, Lee told Reuters the coalition was unlikely to win seats in parliament

The coalition won 4.4 percent of the vote at Saturday's general election and will need to win a disproportionate number of the 250,000 special votes to break the five percent threshold at which parties qualify for seats in parliament.
"I think (specials) will give us a significant lift and make the final scenario even more critically disappointing."
He said his "guestimate" of the level that would justify a recount would be 4.7 percent.
"I have been using that... mainly as an indication that we do not expect the figures to cross (the threshold)," Lee said.
Lee was internal affairs minister in Prime Minister Jim Bolger's cabinet, but was dumped and set up the the Christian Democrats.

He said the coalition would continue in the short term. "But the longer term outcome is a question of what we do in a future election -- what form a party should take and that is a matter yet to be discussed."
He said the coalition came under a lot of unfair criticism on the moral issues and it had trouble "getting on the front foot" on its policy on family values and principles.
"The fact is we were targeted on moral issues."
He said a lot of church support was lost during the campaign after attacks on the party's stand on abortion and homosexuality.
"The homosexual community was central in the attack, they will stay there and will be stronger because of the nature of the parliament... which will be more sympathetic to the homosexual community."
"But all those matters will have to be without Graeme Lee. I am leaving politics when I leave this building tomorrow night."
He would not name an heir apparent but singled out Christian Democrat president David Brown and candidates John Jamieson and Annetta Moran for praise. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
